Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 108, verse 1:

We begin this session with a discussion of the surah: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar (abundance). So pray to your Lord and sacrifice. Indeed, the one who hates you is the one cut off.﴾ [al-Kawthar 1-3].

It has been said that this surah is Meccan, and it has been said that it is Madinan. The Meccan (makki) is that which was revealed before the Prophet's ﷺ migration (hijrah) to Madinah, whether it was revealed in Makkah, in Madinah, or on the way, that is, during a journey. Whatever was revealed after the hijrah is Madinan, and whatever was revealed before it is Meccan. This is the preponderant opinion among the scholars.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, addresses the Prophet ﷺ, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾. Al-Kawthar in the Arabic language means abundant good. Thus the Prophet ﷺ was given by Allah, the Exalted, abundant good in this world and the Hereafter. Among it is the great river in Paradise, from which two spouts pour into his Pool (al-hawd al-mawrud) ﷺ. Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter in taste than honey, and more fragrant than musk. This Pool, on the plain of Resurrection, will be visited by the believers of the Prophet's ﷺ Ummah, and its vessels are like the stars of the sky in number and beauty.[[Muslim (2300 / 36) reported with his chain from Abu Dharr who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the vessels of the Pool?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, its vessels are more numerous than the number of the stars of the sky and its planets. Behold, on a dark, clear night, the vessels of Paradise. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst again after it. Two spouts from Paradise pour into it. Whoever drinks from it will never thirst. Its breadth equals its length, from 'Amman to Aylah. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey."]] Whoever came to his Sharia (path) in this world will come to his Pool in the Hereafter, and whoever did not come to his Sharia will be deprived of it in the Hereafter. We ask Allah to make us and you come to His Pool and give us to drink from it.

Among the abundant good that he ﷺ was given in this world is what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have been given five things that no one before me was given: I was made victorious with terror (cast into the hearts of the enemy) for a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification, so whichever man of my Ummah the time of prayer reaches, let him pray; spoils of war were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given the intercession; and every prophet was sent specifically to his people, while I have been sent to all mankind."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521 / 3), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both); this is the wording of al-Bukhari.]] This is part of the abundant good, because his being sent to all people generally necessitates that he has the greatest number of followers among the prophets, and so it is; he, peace and blessings be upon him, has the most followers.

It is well known that one who guides to good is like one who does good, and this great Ummah, which surpasses other nations in number, was guided by Muhammad ﷺ. Accordingly, the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, will receive a share of the reward of each member of his Ummah, and who can count the Ummah except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

Among the good he was given in the Hereafter is the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud), which includes the great intercession. On the Day of Resurrection, people will be overwhelmed by distress and grief beyond their endurance, so they seek intercession. They come to Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, until they reach the Prophet ﷺ, who stands and intercedes, and Allah judges between the servants by his intercession.[[A reference to the long hadith of intercession reported by al-Bukhari (4476) and Muslim (193 / 322) from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).]] This station will be praised by the first and the last, and it falls under the saying of the Exalted: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isra 79].

So, ﴿al-Kawthar﴾ means what? Abundant good, and among it is the river in Paradise. The river in Paradise is undoubtedly al-Kawthar and is called by that name, but it is not the only thing that Allah gave His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ of good.

Having mentioned His favour upon him with this abundant good, He said: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾, in gratitude to God for this great blessing, that you pray and sacrifice to God. What is meant by prayer here is all prayers, and the first to be included is the prayer coupled with sacrifice, which is the Eid al-Adha prayer; but the verse is general and comprehensive. ﴿Pray to your Lord﴾ covers the obligatory prayers, the voluntary prayers, the Eid prayers, and the Friday prayer.

﴿And sacrifice﴾, i.e., draw near to Him by slaughtering (nahr). Nahr is specific to camels, while dhabh (slaughter) is for cattle and sheep. However, He mentioned nahr because camels are more beneficial than others for the poor (masakin). For this reason the Prophet ﷺ gave them as offerings in his Hajj: he offered one hundred camels, and slaughtered sixty-three of them with his own hand. He gave 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) the rest, and he slaughtered them, and gave away all of their meat except one piece from each camel, which was taken and placed in a pot and cooked, and they ate of its meat and drank of its broth.[[Muslim (1218/147) narrated from the hadith of Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: ... Then he went to the place of sacrifice and slaughtered sixty-three with his own hand, then he gave 'Ali the rest, and he slaughtered them, and made him a partner in his offering. Then he ordered that from every camel a piece be taken, which was placed in a pot and cooked, and the two of them ate of its meat and drank of its broth... the hadith.]] He also commanded that the covers and skins be given in charity.[[Al-Bukhari (1707) and Muslim (1317/349) narrated from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to give in charity the coverings (jilal) of the camels that were slaughtered and their skins. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Jilal (with a kasra on the jim) is the plural of jull (with a damma on the jim), which is the cloth or similar item placed on a camel's back.]] (ﷺ) The command to him is a command to him and to the Ummah. So it is incumbent upon us to make our prayer sincerely for God and to make our sacrifice sincerely for God, just as our Prophet ﷺ was commanded.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.﴾ This is in contrast to the giving of al-Kawthar. He said: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾. ﴿Shani'aka﴾ means your hater (mubghiduka), and al-shana'an means hatred. Among its uses is the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people, because they blocked you from al-Masjid al-Haram, incite you to transgress﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2], i.e., let their hatred not lead you to transgress. ﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾, i.e., let their hatred not lead you to abandon justice. ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8]. So ﴿shani'aka﴾ in His words ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾ means your hater.

﴿Huwa al-abtar﴾: ﴿al-abtar﴾ is an elative form (ism tafdil) from (batara), meaning "cut off", i.e., he is the most severed, cut off from every good. That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh used to say: "Muhammad is abtar (cut off); there is no good in him, no blessing in him, nor in following him, abtar." When his son al-Qasim (may Allah be pleased with him) died, they said: "Muhammad is abtar; he will have no children, and if he had a child, that child would be cut off from lineage." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that the abtar is the hater of the Messenger (ﷺ). He is the abtar, cut off from every good, in whom there is no blessing, and whose life is a regret for him. If this applies to the hater of the Messenger, it also applies to the hater of his legislation. Whoever hates the Messenger's (ﷺ) law, or hates one of the symbols of Islam, or hates any act of worship that people perform in the religion of Islam, is a disbeliever who has left the religion, because of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿That is because they hated what Allah revealed, so He made their deeds fruitless﴾ [Muhammad 9]. Deeds become void only through disbelief. Whoever dislikes the obligation of the prayers is a disbeliever even if he prays, and whoever dislikes the obligation of zakat is a disbeliever even if he gives zakat. But whoever finds it burdensome without disliking it has a characteristic of hypocrisy in him, yet he does not disbelieve. There is a difference between one who finds a thing burdensome and one who dislikes a thing.

Thus this verse contains an explanation of Allah's blessing upon His Messenger (ﷺ) in giving him abundant good, then the command to sincerity toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the prayers and the sacrifice, and likewise in all acts of worship, and then an explanation that whoever hates the Messenger (ﷺ) or hates any part of his law is the one cut off, in whom there is no good and no blessing.
